questions.q: Per this lesson's least-privilege checklist, what should you grant a role when it's first created?
options: As much access as possible, to minimize future grant requests
Only what it needs right now, adding more later when actually requested
Full ACCOUNTADMIN-equivalent access as a starting point
Nothing — roles should never be granted any privileges
questions.explain: Least privilege means granting only what's needed today; it's safer to add access later on request than to over-grant up front and have to claw it back.

questions.q: What problem does a FUTURE grant (e.g. GRANT SELECT ON FUTURE TABLES IN SCHEMA ...) solve?
options: It revokes access to all existing tables
It automatically applies the grant to tables and views created later in that schema, so new objects aren't manually forgotten
It schedules a grant to run at a future date and time
It grants access only to tables that will be deleted
questions.explain: Future grants apply to objects that don't exist yet, so a fast-growing schema doesn't require a manual grant for every new table — eliminating the forgotten-grant problem.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend keeping ACCOUNTADMIN membership to a tiny handful of people and doing day-to-day work as SECURITYADMIN, USERADMIN, or SYSADMIN instead?
options: ACCOUNTADMIN is deprecated and will be removed
ACCOUNTADMIN has the largest blast radius in the account; the other roles can do their jobs without that level of exposure
ACCOUNTADMIN cannot run SELECT statements
There is no actual reason, it's purely a style preference
questions.explain: ACCOUNTADMIN can manage every aspect of the account, including billing — limiting its membership reduces the damage any single compromised or mistaken login can do.

questions.q: What does SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE governance_demo.sales.orders; tell you, as opposed to SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE analyst_role;?
options: They return identical results
SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE shows who currently has access to that specific table; SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE shows everything a given role can do
SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE deletes the table
SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE only works for system-defined roles
questions.explain: The two SHOW GRANTS forms answer opposite questions: what can this role do (TO ROLE) versus who has access to this object (ON TABLE) — both are useful for a routine access audit.
